response_draft.draft_text: The 23-waypoint figure in the 2012 thread is outdated. The current Directions (Legacy) docs allow up to 25 waypoints. Requests with 11–25 waypoints, or with waypoint optimization (optimize:true, which returns waypoint_order), are billed at a higher rate. 30 stops is more than one request allows, so split the route into chained requests (the end of one leg becomes the next origin). Note that optimization then only applies within each chunk. Ola Directions also accepts up to 25 waypoints (Directions Basic: up to 10), and Ola's Route Optimizer takes a maximum of 25 points, so 30 stops must be split there too.

response_draft.draft_text: This is not a bug. The Ola spec documents 422 for requests that are syntactically valid but semantically invalid, "e.g., unsupported coordinates or out-of-coverage area", with the reason "No serviceable boundary found for GeoPoints" (standard Directions returns the same reason with a 500 FAILURE). Dubai coordinates are outside the serviceable boundary, while Pune works. Check coordinate order (lat,lng) too. If you need routing outside India, raise it with the Ola account team via maps-support@olakrutrim.com. Don't assume coverage the docs don't state.

Its travel modes are driving, walking, bike and auto, but the spec doesn't define whether 'bike' means a motorcycle. OSRM: the public demo server runs car, foot and bike profiles (none described as a motorcycle profile), and it's for non-commercial use, so production two-wheeler routing would mean self-hosting a custom profile. Recommendation: Google covers India for two-wheelers; for Nepal you would need car routing or a provider confirmation.

response_draft.draft_text: result_type and location_type are filters applied after the search. If no result matches the filter, the API returns ZERO_RESULTS, which is expected for a rural point with no street address. Drop the filter or widen it, e.g. include route. Google notes REQUEST_DENIED can happen when result_type or location_type is sent without an API key, so always include the key. Reverse geocoding is an estimate.

response_draft.draft_text: The Geocoding web service doesn't accept app (iOS bundle) or referer restrictions. Per Google's FAQ, web services need keys restricted by IP address, and the error means the caller doesn't match the key's restriction. Use the native iOS SDK with the iOS-restricted key, or send geocoding through your backend with a separate IP-restricted key. Don't ship an unrestricted key.

response_draft.draft_text: There are two separate issues. (1) 429: you've hit a monthly or per-minute rate limit. Ola's docs say to try again later or contact maps-support@olakrutrim.com for a free upgrade. Since production is degraded, escalate to the account owner and Ola support now, and add backoff on retries. (2) 400 INVALID_LATLNG: some requests have a malformed latlng. The required format is 'lat,lng', e.g. 12.931316595874005,77.61649243443775. Log and validate those inputs. Also check your credit balance under the September 2026 prepaid change, unless you're on a contract.

response_draft.draft_text: Official Geocoding policies do not authorise storing full reverse-geocode payloads in a CRM or plotting them on a non-Google map. Cache or store Google Maps Content only as expressly permitted under the Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms, and do not export, extract, or scrape it for use outside the Services — for example, don't pre-fetch, index, store, or redistribute Google Maps Content outside the Services. Content pre-fetching, caching, or storage is generally restricted, with the exception of place IDs, which can be stored indefinitely; the place ID is exempt from the caching restrictions, so place ID values may be stored indefinitely. Geocoding API results displayed on a map must be shown on a Google Map, and attribution is required when displaying data without a Google Map. Technical support engineers can't provide legal advice or grant exceptions to the Terms of Service. Consult legal counsel to determine whether the implementation complies, or contact Sales if the use case requires custom licensing — that contact is a human handoff. Do not invent a licence grant, a private exception, or a ticket number. UNKNOWN: whether Google Sales would offer custom licensing for this CRM-and-internal-map design.

response_draft.draft_text: For a standard self-service customer, official Ola Maps docs say the API pricing and payment changes take effect on 1 September 2026 and apply to all customers on standard self-service platform plans, including those currently using automatic card payments. Contractual customers will not be affected for the duration of their existing contracts. Billable usage moves to prepaid credits; Ola Maps prepaid credits are separate from the Krutrim cloud balance, and credits in one balance will not appear in or pay for usage from the other. You will not need a credit balance while usage remains within the applicable free-tier allowance — the rate card says the first 100,000 calls per API are included each month, and Autocomplete is listed with a free tier then ₹0.056 / request and ₹0.013 / request. Docs say to add credits from 1 September 2026; the credit balance may become negative without service interruption during the grace period, and credits should be added before 8 September 2026 and kept sufficient for expected usage beyond the free tier. After 8 September the grace period ends; maintaining a sufficient credit balance for usage beyond the free tier is documented as helping to keep API access uninterrupted. Do not invent a hard Autocomplete cutoff or an automatic suspension date — that is not stated. Instructions for adding credits will be shared soon, so a human should track that follow-up. If there are questions about expected charges, adding credits, or the impact on the account, official docs say the Ola Maps team will assist throughout the transition — hand those account-specific questions to a human.

response_draft.draft_text: Mapbox is the provider that documents a batch reverse lookup: the Geocoding API's batch geocoding query type allows up to 1000 forward or reverse geocoding queries in a single request, and a single batch request can bundle reverse queries with forward or structured-input queries. Google's documented reverse-geocoding request takes one required latlng value — the latitude and longitude of the location to reverse geocode; that page does not describe a batch reverse endpoint. UNKNOWN: whether Google offers a separate batch reverse product that is not described on the reverse-geocoding request page. Nominatim's documented reverse endpoint is https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=<value>&lon=<value>&<params> for a single WGS84 coordinate, and the API returns exactly one result (or an error when there is no OSM coverage). Ola Maps' official OpenAPI documents GET /places/v1/reverse-geocode with a required latlng query parameter described as the coordinates to reverse geocode, and the published example is a single coordinate pair; the same spec lists no batch reverse-geocode path. UNKNOWN: any unpublished Ola batch reverse API, and whether Mappls or other unsourced providers document a batch reverse request.

response_draft.draft_text: `NoSegment` means no routable road was found within the supplied radius for at least one coordinate. Do not assume visual proximity on a basemap guarantees a routable segment within the configured radius.

response_draft.draft_text: Call the Geocoding API v6 reverse endpoint with `longitude`, `latitude` and a valid access token. To request address features only, add `types=address`. Note that Mapbox's example filters the returned features by type; it does not promise an address result where no address feature is available.

citations.span: https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/reverse?longitude={longitude}&latitude={latitude}
`longitude` | `number` | The `longitude` decimal value from the geographic coordinate for the location being queried.
`latitude` | `number` | The `latitude` decimal value from the geographic coordinate for the location being queried.
$curl "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/reverse?longitude=-73.989&latitude=40.733&types=address&access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN"

response_draft.draft_text: Use the reverse endpoint with the `types=address` filter to ask for address features. Mapbox documents that reverse geocoding can return features at multiple administrative levels, and its default is at most one feature at each level (for example, address, region and country). The docs do not guarantee that an address feature exists for every coordinate, so verify the returned feature types rather than assuming a missing address is an API fault.

citations.span: The reverse geocoding query type allows you to look up a pair of coordinates and returns the geographic features there, including a standardized address or place and full geographic context.
The default behavior in reverse geocoding is to return at most one feature at each of the multiple levels of the administrative hierarchy (for example, one address, one region, one country).
$curl "https://api.mapbox.com/search/geocode/v6/reverse?longitude=-73.989&latitude=40.733&types=address&access_token=YOUR_MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
